newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-SCOTLAND SEEK REAL WIN IN ESTONIA REPLAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCOTLAND SEEK REAL WIN IN ESTONIA REPLAY.

text.p: Scotland will seek to extend their lead at the top of their World Cup qualifying group against Estonia in Monaco on Tuesday in a replay of a game scrapped last year when Estonia failed to show up.

Estonian coach Teitur Thordarson plans to send his young team into attack hoping for an upset despite what he fears is Scottish skill in set pieces and in the air, including tall Everton striker Duncan Ferguson.

"We're a well organised team and everyone knows their job and I am not so sure we will lose, "said Thordarson, who added "We have no injury worries and have nothing to lose." But that sounded an optimistic evaluation about a team who were beaten by Lebanon in their last match.
The match is being played in the Mediterranean
principality of Monaco after Estonia failed to show up to the original game in Tallinn in October, where the kick-off was brought forward after Scotland complained about the floodlights.

Scotland kicked off alone and were originally awarded a 3-0 victory after a surreal game that lasted three seconds. Estonia secured a replay, and Monaco was chosen after suggestions of sending the teams to Cyprus or even Azerbaijan.
Thordarson said the Estonians, deprived of a local crowd for the game, were not smarting for revenge after the farce in Tallinn. "It won't make much difference," he said.

Scotland currently heads World Cup qualifying group four with seven points, ahead of Austria on goal difference after three games apiece. A victory would extend Scotland's lead to three clear points and if they follow up an expected win in Monaco with home wins against Estonia and Austria on March 29 and April 2, they would be in a very healthy position to qualify for the finals.
"This match is important because a victory would put us in a strong position in the group," said Scotland's John Collins of local club Monaco, the player least put out by the change of venue.
He said that the game in Tallinn, watched in its entirety by millions of people around the world in television replays, had been a "nightmare".

And the game could give Scotland a chance to overcome a recent drought of goals -- manager Craig Brown is searching for a winning combination up front with just three goals in its World Cup qualifiers so far. Ferguson has been on form recently, with five goals in his last nine games for his club, but has yet to score for Scotland after a debut in 1992.
Brown has been spoilt for choice, even though Craig Burley of Chelsea, Darren Jackson of Hibernian, QPR's John Spencer and Alan McLaren of Rangers are out of the original squad because of injury.

Estonia (from): Mart Poom, Martin Kaalma, Sergei Hohlov-Simson, Marek Lemsalu, Gert Olesk, Urmas Kirs, Urmas Rooba, Martin Reim, Viktor Alonen, Meelis Rooba, Marko Kristal, Indrek Zelinksi, Liivo Leetma, Andres Oper, Argo Arbeiter, Raivo Nommik, Janek Meet, Mati Pari.
Scotland (probable): Andy Goram, Jackie McNamara, Colin Hendry, Colin Calderwood, Tosh McKinlay, Ian Ferguson, Gary McAllister, John Collins, John McGinlay, Duncan Ferguson, Kevin Gallacher
